subject: HelixHealth: evidence path for KMS/BYO, SSO logs and audit window exception
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixhealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit evidence and KMS/BYO requirements - initial ask

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. To recap HelixHealth's blocking items for our security review: 1) evidence that KMS/BYO key rotations are logged and retainable for 7 years; 2) a mapping between SSO session IDs and internal user IDs (we need at least 90 days of session logs, indexed by user); 3) an audit window SLA exception for dedicated deployments while we complete our SOC review (we need a committed path and timeline).

Can you confirm what evidence artifacts Redwood can provide (raw logs, indexed exports, or signed attestations)? Attached a short requirements doc. We are hoping for a mutual action plan this week so our legal/compliance can sign off.

Attachment: Helix_Audit_Requirements_v1.pdf

Best,
Evan Brooks
Head of Compliance, HelixHealth
security@helixhealth.com
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit evidence and KMS/BYO requirements - initial ask

Evan — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned that this is high priority. Quick triage from our side:

- What we can offer quickly: signed attestation describing current KMS rotation and audit-log retention + a one-time indexed export for the last 90 days.
- What will take engineering work: live index linking SSO session IDs to userids for rolling 7-year retention, and a persistent 7-year retention SLA.

Request to Helix: can you confirm the minimum acceptable artifacts for legal sign-off (attestation + 90-day export vs. longer)? That will let us scope the MAP.

Internal ask: Priyom / Irene — please confirm feasibility and rough ETA for: 1) one-off 90-day export of KMS rotation entries and session logs; 2) estimate for adding a retention extension path (7-year indexed retention) and any gating product work. Ben, please advise on operational evidence we should include.

Proposed next step: I will draft a MAP with milestone dates once we have estimates.

Thanks — Naomie
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Safety (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixhealth.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit evidence and KMS/BYO requirements - initial ask

Naomi / Priyom — technical triage below. Keeping bullets concise to surface tradeoffs quickly.

- One-off 90-day export: feasible. We can generate a compressed export (NDJSON) of KMS key rotation events + SSO session logs within 3 business days. Need approval on fields to include (timestamps, key_id, operation, principal, request_id, region).

- 7-year indexed retention: medium effort. Two parts: (A) storage/backfill + cost accounting; (B) index linking session_id -> user_id that survives retention period (privacy review required). Rough ETA: 10-12 weeks to implement as a platform feature with automated retention apron, assuming prioritization in release pipeline.

- SLA exception path: we can offer a timeboxed SLA exception (e.g., dedicated deployment with manual escrow snapshots and signed attestations) as a near-term mitigation. That reduces code changes but requires Ops runbooks and legal sign-off.

Attachment: implementation_estimate.xlsx

Open questions for product/security owners:
1) Are we comfortable storing long-lived session -> user mappings (PII concerns)? If not, we can store hashed identifiers with salt managed by Helix (BYO-hash).
2) For the export format, does Helix need JSON vs. CSV?

I'll prepare a short runbook draft once we pick the mitigation path.

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance Engineering
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit evidence and KMS/BYO requirements - initial ask

Quick ops perspective:

- We can deliver the one-off 90-day export and a signed attestation within 4 business days if fields are confirmed. That will include request_ids, timestamps, key_id, and rotation reason metadata.
- For the longer-term retention, a pragmatic mitigation is: keep full fidelity logs for 90 days; for 7-year retention, store compressed event digests (hashes) plus an indexed pointer table Helix can provide salt for. This satisfies auditability without exposing raw PII.
- Runbook items: who triggers the export, verification checklist, chain-of-custody email templates. I can draft those.

I'll sync with Infra on cost delta; rough ops estimate is extra S3/Tiered storage + indexing work: expected incremental cost $X/month (will confirm).

Ben Carter
Security Operations
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@helixhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit evidence and KMS/BYO requirements - initial ask

Evan — thanks to you and team for the clarity. Consolidating the MAP below for legal sign-off and product prioritization. Please confirm if this is acceptable to Helix and we'll put the DocuSign SLA draft in motion.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
- Day 0 (this week): Redwood provides signed attestation + confirm export schema. (Deliverable: attestation PDF, export schema doc)
- Day 4 (by Aug 6): One-off 90-day export (NDJSON) delivered, Ops runbook attached, signed chain-of-custody email. (Deliverable: export archive, runbook)
- Week 4 (by Aug 27): Decide on long-term approach: Helix chooses between (A) BYO-hash index for 7-year retention or (B) Redwood-managed indexed retention (costed).
- Week 12 (approx Sep 21): If (B) selected and prioritized, Redwood delivers retention feature beta/ops, otherwise, implement agreed escrow pattern and continuing attestation cadence.

Open asks to Helix: confirm preferred export fields and whether hashed user identifiers are acceptable for long-term retention.

Action items (owners):
- Naomi: prepare DocuSign temp SLA and attestations (attached draft) — will send by EOD.
- Priyom: confirm product prioritization and feasibility; prepare a short PRD stub if option (B) is chosen.
- Irene: finalize runbook template and privacy notes on hashed identifiers.
- Ben: prepare cost memo for retention options.

If Helix can confirm acceptance of the MAP and export schema by EOD tomorrow, we'll route the temp-SLA to legal for signature.

Thanks — Naomie
